ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This pedigree chart shows three generations of individuals. At the top of generation I, an affected female (black circle) is married to an unaffected male (blank square). In generation II, multiple children and their spouses can be seen, including affected males (black squares) and affected females (black circles), as well as unaffected males and females. In generation III, affected individuals also continue to appear, including affected females and affected males; on the right side, an affected male in generation II married to an unaffected female has an affected son, suggesting father-to-son transmission. Reasoning: This trait appears in generations I, II, and III, showing continuous transmission across generations, which is more consistent with dominant inheritance rather than recessive inheritance. Affected individuals include males and females, indicating that it is not limited to one sex. The figure shows a case in which an affected father transmits it to an affected son, excluding X-linked inheritance; at the same time, females are also affected, excluding Y-linked inheritance. Combining continuous transmission across generations, both males and females being affected, and the phenomenon of male-to-male transmission, the most likely mode of inheritance is autosomal dominant inheritance.

raw_record.question_text: Name the most likely mode of inheritance in the following pedigree:

method.method_draft: Describe the pedigree visually generation by generation, marking which males and females are shaded. Then test inheritance patterns: because the trait appears in every generation, affects both males and females, and includes male-to-male transmission from an affected father to an affected son, classify it as autosomal rather than sex-linked and dominant rather than recessive. Conclude the most likely mode is autosomal dominant.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：该谱系图显示三代个体。第 I 代顶部是一名受累女性（黑色圆形）与一名未受累男性（空白方形）婚配。第 II 代可见多名子女及其配偶，其中既有受累男性（黑色方形），也有受累女性（黑色圆形），同时也有未受累的男性和女性。第 III 代中也继续出现受累个体，包括受累女性和受累男性；右侧可见一名第 II 代受累男性与未受累女性婚配后生出一名受累儿子，提示存在父亲到儿子的传递。推理：该性状在第 I、II、III 代均出现，呈连续世代传递，更符合显性遗传而非隐性遗传。受累者包括男性和女性，说明不是限于某一性别。图中存在受累父亲传给受累儿子的情况，排除 X 连锁遗传；同时女性也受累，排除 Y 连锁遗传。综合连续世代传递、男女均可受累以及男传男现象，最可能的遗传方式是常染色体显性遗传。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct pedigree-pattern route: infer the inheritance mode from vertical transmission, sex distribution, and father-to-son transmission rather than calculating genotype probabilities.
planner_metadata.image_role: First describe the image: identify shaded symbols as affected and unshaded as unaffected; note an affected female in generation I mated with an unaffected male, affected individuals of both sexes in generation II, affected individuals appearing again in generation III, and at least one affected male with an affected son on the right side of the pedigree.
planner_metadata.text_role: Read the prompt only to know the task is to name the most likely inheritance mode from the displayed pedigree; there are no additional textual constraints or answer options to use.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard pedigree rules: autosomal dominant traits usually show vertical transmission across successive generations, affect males and females similarly, can be transmitted father-to-son, and often produce affected offspring from an affected heterozygous parent with an unaffected spouse. Father-to-son transmission rules out X-linked inheritance, and continuous multi-generation appearance argues against autosomal recessive as the most likely pattern.
